title: The Pain of Missing Home
subtitle: The Compassare swaying in the wind, the water wheel turning on the riverbank—these are the familiar scenes that people long for.

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: Ms. Vertin, it seems all the passengers are gathered in the lobby.
The group has finally arrived at the cruise ship lobby. The place is a mess.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: We've lost too much time. A lot of people have put on masks while we were locked up.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We'll need to round up the ones that are still conscious!

items.speaker: Helmsman Charlie
items.text: Sure!
The hastily assembled rescue team leaps into action, breaking up rising quarrels and separating the crowd members fighting over masks.

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: Damn, more contenders! Like we don't have enough people wrestling for a mask!

items.speaker: Guest II
items.text: Give me that mask, asshole!

items.speaker: Guest II
items.text: I'm joining Manus Vindictae! I will take the trial!
Clearly, any semblance of onboard etiquette has been long abandoned.

items.speaker: Crew Member I
items.text: Sir, I believe you may be too weak to endure the trial! You should leave this valuable opportunity to someone who will be more useful to Captain Grace!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Please put the masks down, everyone! This isn't the way to survive!

items.speaker: Guest III
items.text: Give it to me! That mask belongs to me!

items.speaker: Guest III
items.text: Ms. Grace smiled at me once! She must like me! She'll want me to join her!

items.speaker: Crew Member II
items.text: I just don't want to be killed by this "Storm" thing.

items.speaker: Crew Member II
items.text: *sob* I don't want to die.
The helmsmen dip and dive through the crowd as they administer sedatogens to the almost delirious passengers.

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: Get back to your senses, people!

items.speaker: Helmsman Esam
items.text: If I were you, I'd have thrown these creepy masks into the sea the moment I saw them!
The Nukutai survivors watch the nearby rescue operation from afar.
Thanks to Grace's kindness, their situation appears far "brighter" than the other guests.
But not all of them share their newfound faith.

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: Selone, you must put on the mask, please. For our people. It's not scary, I promise.

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: Would you rather be captured by those outsiders?!

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: Go to the captain's room, Toa.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: You passed your trial. I'm sure the captain and our people there need you more than I do.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: I must stay here to look after Kitiona, little Pita, and our friends who still seem to be lost.

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: What is wrong with you, Selone? All you need to do is put on the mask!
Selone breaks free of Toa's grip, nearly falling to the floor as she does so.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: I'm sorry, Toa. I think Fatutu was right to have second thoughts.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: Look at all the people who have put on the mask. Now, tell me how many of them have survived?
Following Selone's tear-filled gaze, countless failures of the trial lie sprawled on the floor.
Nukutai, Australians, Italians ...
Sailors, merchants, tourists ...

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: And what, you're afraid? Is this really more important than bringing our people home?!
The storm outside continues to batter the ship.
The lobby, however, grows increasingly silent.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: You have changed. The Toa I knew would never have dared to ask me such a foolish question.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: Haven't you heard their cries?

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: You need to think of the future, Selone, the new, beautiful homeland we're going to recover! We could live peacefully once more. We could—
His tears mix with the viscous black liquid of the mask as they drip onto the floor.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: Please stop, Toa. I'm sorry.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: When I see how tainted and twisted your Spirit Shell has become, I can't. I won't.
Selone crumples to the floor, her voice barely a whisper.
Sonetto spots them among the crowd.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I recognize her. That's Ms. Selone!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, I think they need assistance!
She rushes toward the Nukutai survivors.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto, watch out!

items.speaker: Nukutai Believer I
items.text: *roar* To ... a new world!
Narrowly dodging the attack, Sonetto looks up in surprise.

items.speaker: Nukutai Believer II
items.text: ... *roar* ... *roar*
Beneath their cold bronze masks, viscous black fluid seeps from the Nukutai believers' eyes and mouths.
Their limbs have twisted into grotesque shapes, and they mutter to themselves, as though tormented by an unending pain.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto, get ready to use those sedatogens.
Their frenzy subsides as the suffering individuals drift into slumber.

items.speaker: Delirious Believer
items.text: *roar* I ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Pardon me for this, please.
She sprays a dose of sedatogen over them.

items.speaker: Delirious Believer
items.text: Home ... home ...
Unfortunately, the sedatogen seems to have little effect on those under the control of the masks.

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: What're you doing to my people?!

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: I won't let you hurt them!
Toa stands vigilantly before Sonetto, shielding the unconscious Manus believers.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Ms. Vertin, Ms. Sonetto, we're back!
Fatutu comes rushing over.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Selone, Toa, are you alright?

items.speaker: Toa
items.text: Tutu?
Their encounter brings little joy.
Toa, instinctively touching the mask clasped to his face, takes a few steps back.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: I'm so glad to see you unharmed, Fatutu. But our friends ...

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I know what happened, Selone. Barcarola told me everything when she got me out.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I've made up my mind now. We can't wear their masks, Selone. We never should have agreed to their so-called revenge plan.
The Manus believers seem to latch onto her words, reacting as though they are a shot of adrenaline.

items.speaker: Delirious Believer
items.text: Revenge ...! *roar*
Toa leaps forward, the ragged claws tearing through his arm as he shields his childhood friend once again.

items.speaker: Selone
items.text: Toa!

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: No! No! Why is this happening?
Blood splatters before her eyes, painting the lobby wall crimson.
The believer's appetite for vengeance has only grown stronger.

items.speaker: Delirious Believer
items.text: Retribution ...! *roar*

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: They seem to be more frantic than ever before! Timekeeper, I suggest increasing the dosage of sedatogens!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The mask's influence has wormed its way deep into their brains. I'm afraid sedatogens won't be able to awaken their consciousness any longer.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They need something that reaches into their soul.
The Manus believers are determined to destroy everything in their path.
As they surge forward, the crowd is pushed back. Barcarola is caught in the center of the chaos.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Isn't there something I can do?
The wails, the cries, and the pounding rain outside nearly overwhelm her. Amidst the chaos, her bow slips out of her hand.
*thwack*
She jumps at the sound.
Stop playing with that atrocious toy of yours and pay attention to the class, Barcarola!
Music is a language that moves us on to a deeper level than any other, transcending both culture, place, and time.
Whoever you are, and wherever you go, it will always stir the depths of your soul!
No need to remember. No need to think.
Familiar, simple tones flow from her Crackling Box.
A soft, indescribable melody washes over Fatutu.
This song is both strange yet intimate. Where is it from?
Is it from the Cremona that Barcarola talked about? The helmsmen's spontaneous sing-song? Or from Meli's traditional bonfire festival?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: We're not so different deep down, are we?

items.speaker: Surprised Guest
items.text: Huh? What's that sound? Violins, piano, cellos, double bass, and flutes!

items.speaker: Confused Guest
items.text: But violins? She hates violins!

items.speaker: Dismayed Guest
items.text: I-I want to go home! *sob*

items.speaker: Delirious Believer
items.text: *roar* ... *roar*

items.speaker: Delirious Believer
items.text: *roar* Nukutaeao ...
Her people raise their hands helplessly, clawing at the air.
Tears blur her vision, but her thoughts only grow clearer.
Though her hands are trembling, she gently lifts the harmonica to her lips.
Her quivering lips blow a gentle rhythm into the harmonica.
A new melody joins the ensemble.
The islander and the musician exchange a glance, and, with no baton nor words, music flows between them like an ancient, joyful river.
The black liquid stills, no longer seeping from the masks of the helpless.
The melody echoes through the lobby, gently closing the eyes of the tormented believers.
Toa's raised hands finally fall, as though succumbing to a deep sleep.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: It's over now, dear friends.
Barcarola nervously wrings her hands.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: I'm sorry, Fatutu. I didn't expect my song to put your people in this state. I only wanted to help.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: You did. You're the greatest musician I've ever seen.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: But, your friends, they've—

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: They've gone home.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: But ...
The lightly trembling shoulders before her suddenly feel unfamiliar.
Had those fragile, tender shoulders always been so brave and resolute?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Look at the shining, pristine Spirit Shells around their necks. That is a sign. It tells us that their souls are at peace.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: That our friends lived a full and honest life.
Wiping her tears, Fatutu gets to her feet and starts to gently collect her lost people's Spirit Shells. She can still feel their warmth in her palm.

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: Fatutu!
Before the warmth of the Spirit Shells can fade, Kamuta strides into the lobby, his demeanor cold.
